lines.text: But computers find each other by number, not by name.
So your device asks a resolver: a helper that does the looking-up for you.
The trick? A name is read from right to left.
First, a root server. It doesn't know the address, but it knows who runs dot com.
The dot com server doesn't know either, but it knows who's in charge of example.
The resolver hands the number back, and your browser connects. Usually in a blink.
It also keeps a copy, for as long as the record's time to live allows.
So next time, the answer is already there.
